speaker: Doctor
text: I notice you have a yellowish coloring to your skin and eyes, along with some agitation. When did you first notice this yellowing, and have you experienced any abdominal pain or changes in your stool or urine color?

speaker: Patient
text: 20-year-old male. The patient was previously healthy and has been brought to the emergency department due to agitation over the past 24 hours. Family members have noticed a yellowish coloring of his skin and eyes over the past week. The patient has a history of occasional cocaine and ecstasy use, and drinks alcohol socially on weekends. The patient also admits to high-risk sexual behaviors without using appropriate protection.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your recent high-risk sexual history and symptoms of jaundice and agitation, have you noticed any abdominal pain, particularly in the upper right side, or any darkening of your urine? I also need to know if you have had any recent unexplained weight loss or fever.

speaker: Doctor

text: Given the markedly elevated bilirubin and transaminases with normal Hepatitis B and C serologies, I need to rule out other causes of acute liver failure. Have you experienced any fever, right-upper-quadrant pain, or dark urine, and do you recall any recent ingestion of potentially toxic substances or herbal supplements?

speaker: Patient

speaker: Doctor
